cards.text: This letter comes from a writer who calls himself the elder, and he's writing to one man, Gaius. The elder calls him beloved and says he loves him in the truth. If somebody greeted ME like that, I'd bake them cookies for a MONTH.

cards.question: The elder opens by praying that Gaius will prosper and enjoy good health in every way. What does the elder say is already prospering?

cards.text: Some brothers came and testified about Gaius's devotion to the truth, and Gaius is still walking in it. The elder takes that news like a man pulling a PERFECT batch out of the oven.

cards.question: The elder is overjoyed by that report about Gaius. What does the elder say gives him no greater joy?

answers.text: Hearing his children walk in the truth
Seeing his churches grow in number
Hearing his letters were read aloud

cards.text: Then the elder tells Gaius he's FAITHFUL in what he's doing for the brothers. Friend, I've had oven timers that couldn't make it through one batch.

cards.question: The elder calls Gaius faithful in what he's doing for the brothers. What does the elder say makes it especially so?

answers.text: They are old friends of his

cards.text: These brothers are traveling through, and they've testified to the church about Gaius's love. Friend, that beats any five-star review.

cards.question: The traveling brothers Gaius has been helping are moving on. How does the elder say Gaius will do well to send them on their way?

answers.text: In a manner worthy of God
In a manner worthy of kings
In a manner pleasing to the church

cards.text: Here's why it matters: the elder says these brothers went out on behalf of the Name, accepting nothing from the Gentiles.

cards.question: True or false: The elder says that supporting men like these makes us fellow workers for the truth.

cards.text: Now the letter turns, friend. The elder says he has written to the church about this, and then he brings up a man named Diotrephes, who loves to be first.

cards.question: The elder has written to the church. True or false: Diotrephes accepts the elder's instruction.

cards.text: The elder doesn't let it slide. He says, "So if I come, I will call attention to his malicious slander against us…"

cards.question: Slander isn't enough for Diotrephes. The elder says he refuses to ___ the brothers.
Diotrephes won't welcome the traveling brothers. What does he do to people in the church who want to welcome them?

answers.text: Forbids them and puts them out
Warns them but lets them go ahead
Asks the elder to settle it by letter

cards.question: After the trouble with Diotrephes, the elder turns back to Gaius. He tells Gaius not to imitate what is evil, but what is ___.

cards.text: The elder says the one who does good is of God, and the one who does evil has not seen God. Then a new name comes up, Demetrius, not the silversmith in Ephesus (Acts 19:24), and friend, this report sounds VERY different.

cards.question: Demetrius has a good testimony from everyone, and from the truth itself. True or false: The elder refuses to add his own testimony for Demetrius.

cards.text: The elder's got many things left to write, but he'd rather skip the pen and ink and see Gaius soon, face to face. Friend, the elder is NOT a group chat guy.

cards.question: The elder signs off wishing Gaius peace and sending greetings from the friends with him. True or false: He asks Gaius to greet each of the friends where Gaius is by name.
